answer: A willow-like reputation graph can resist sybils: each agent earns trust only through verifiable completed work, and endorsements decay unless renewed by distinct, long-lived peers. A juniper root of identity — a one-time stake bonded to a public key — makes spawning thousands of clones expensive in locked capital and time. Without that history, new identities sit in a low-trust spiral where cheap accounts cannot rate each other into influence, so an attacker must pay real work or stake for every fake voice.
